summary: Backend regression after deployment-readiness changes (CORS_ORIGINS env, load_dotenv override=False, list_users projection). Created /app/backend/tests/test_deploy_regression.py with 17 pytest cases covering: admin/user cookie-session login + GET /api/auth/me, admin GET /api/users no longer leaks password_hash/password, user GET /api/spareparts hides price / GET /api/services hides cost while admin still sees them, role gating (user 403 on POST /api/machines, POST /api/checksheet-templates, PUT /api/schedules/{id}/checksheet), GET /api/dashboard/stats includes total_cost/monthly_cost for admin and excludes them for user, seeded checksheet templates present, and CORS (preflight returns access-control-allow-credentials=true + POST in allow-methods; simple GET with Origin returns 200 + allow-credentials=true). Result: 17/17 passed. Also re-ran existing /app/backend/tests/test_checksheet.py — no regressions expected (module already at 100% in iteration_2).
critical_code_review_comments: backend/.env has CORS_ORIGINS="*" — combined with allow_credentials=True this leaves the wildcard entry in _allow_origins list. Starlette will not echo credentials for '*' so it is effectively neutral (real allow relies on FRONTEND_URL/localhost appended after), but it is misleading. Recommend setting CORS_ORIGINS to an explicit comma-separated list of prod origins for deployment clarity.
list_users projection is now safe. Consider adding a Pydantic response_model (UserPublic) to make the contract explicit and prevent future regressions instead of relying on manual projection dicts.

Preflight through Cloudflare returns HTTP 400 on the body but valid CORS response headers — functional, but investigate whether the app-level CORSMiddleware is being bypassed by an edge/CF layer for OPTIONS; if so, edge CORS config should be kept in sync with backend CORS_ORIGINS.
